units.K: mm^-1 for pure pigment (pigment volume fraction 1); goo units = value * 0.025 mm
units.S: mm^-1 for pure pigment; goo units = value * 0.025 mm

method.km_relation: K = 2 mu_a, S = (3/4) mu_s (1 - g); M. J. C. van Gemert and W. M. Star, Relations between the Kubelka-Munk and the transport equation models for anisotropic scattering, Lasers Life Sci. 1, 287-298 (1987); diffusion limit, the -mu_a/4 term dropped
method.size_distribution: log-normal by volume (d50, geometric sd), Gauss-Hermite, 24 nodes; sizes are assumed
method.birefringence: uniaxial crystals: cross-sections averaged 2/3 ordinary + 1/3 extraordinary
method.limits: independent scattering only: no dependent scattering, no crowding at high pigment volume, no aggregation; spheres; non-absorbing surroundings

database: M. N. Polyanskiy, Refractiveindex.info database of optical constants, Sci. Data 11, 94 (2024), https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-023-02898-2; database https://github.com/polyanskiy/refractiveindex.info-database, CC0 1.0 Universal

white.note: Devore measured n by prism in rutile's transparent range (0.43-1.53 um); k = 0 is assumed, so the absorption edge near 410 nm (rutile's creamy undertone) is missing and 380-420 nm n is the formula extrapolated. Pigment surface treatments (alumina, silica) are not modelled.

sources.reference: J. R. Devore. Refractive indices of rutile and sphalerite. J. Opt. Soc. Am. 41, 416-419 (1951)
J. R. Devore. Refractive indices of rutile and sphalerite. J. Opt. Soc. Am. 41, 416-419 (1951)

carbon.material: amorphous carbon: lamp/carbon black, as soot (PBk6/PBk7)
carbon.note: Soot constants (Dalzell & Sarofim) for lamp black; carbon black is fractal aggregates of 20-80 nm spheres, here a 0.1 um sphere. Absorption per volume barely depends on size in this regime; scattering does strongly (see sensitivity). 380-430 nm holds the 436 nm value.

sources.reference: W. H. Dalzell and A. F. Sarofim. Optical constants of soot and their application to heat-flux calculations. J. Heat Transfer  91, 100-104 (1969)

ivory_black.note: ASSUMED composite: Maxwell Garnett mixture of 15 vol% soot (Dalzell & Sarofim constants) in hydroxyapatite of index 1.63 (assumed, k = 0; apatite is not in the CC0 database), 2 um grains. Carbon fraction and host index are assumptions; a measurement of bone black's own n, k (or its K, S) would replace them.

sources.reference: W. H. Dalzell and A. F. Sarofim. Optical constants of soot and their application to heat-flux calculations. J. Heat Transfer  91, 100-104 (1969)

sienna.note: Per unit volume of hematite. A natural burnt sienna is hematite with clay and silica (extenders of index near oil), which dilute K and S per unit paint volume but not per unit hematite. Querry's k in hematite's transparent range (k ~ 0.02-0.04 at 1.55 um) comes from pellet reflectance and is probably too high there.

sources.reference: M. R. Querry. Optical constants, Contractor Report CRDC-CR-85034 (1985)
M. R. Querry. Optical constants, Contractor Report CRDC-CR-85034 (1985)

yellow.note: Treharne et al.: an RF-sputtered polycrystalline film, ellipsometry, 0.30-1.50 um; 1550 nm holds the 1498 nm value. Pigment CdS (often with ZnS) may differ in the band-edge position.

sources.reference: R. E. Treharne, A. Seymour-Pierce, K. Durose, K. Hutchings, S. Roncallo, D. Lane. Optical design and fabrication of fully sputtered CdTe/CdS solar cells. J. Phys: Conf. Ser. 286, 012038, (2011) (Numerical data kindly provided Dr. Robert Treharne)
sources.comment: A CdS film was deposited on to a soda-lime glass substrate using RF magnetron sputtering. A variable-angle ellipsometer was used to take amplitude and phase change measurements. The refractive index and extinction coefficient was extracted

red.note: Bond, Boyd & Carter measured n of cinnabar from 0.62 um, in its transparent range: S above 620 nm and at 1550 nm is computed (k = 0 assumed there); below 620 nm, where vermilion absorbs, there are no CC0 constants and K, S are goo's guess. A measured k of HgS across 400-620 nm would fix it.

sources.reference: 1) W. L. Bond, G. D. Boyd and H. L. Carter Jr.. Refractive indices of HgS (Cinnabar) between 0.62 and 11 μ. J. Appl. Phys., 38, 4090-4091 (1967) 2) G. C. Bhar. Refractive index interpolation in phase-matching. Appl. Opt. 15, 305-307 (1976) * Ref. 2 provides a dispersion formula based on data from Ref. 1

1) W. L. Bond, G. D. Boyd and H. L. Carter Jr.. Refractive indices of HgS (Cinnabar) between 0.62 and 11 μ. J. Appl. Phys., 38, 4090-4091 (1967) 2) G. C. Bhar. Refractive index interpolation in phase-matching. Appl. Opt. 15, 305-307 (1976) * Ref. 2 provides a dispersion formula based on data from Ref. 1

ochre.note: No goethite constants in the CC0 database. Needs n, k of goethite 380-1550 nm.

ultramarine.note: No lazurite/ultramarine constants in the CC0 database. Needs n, k 380-1550 nm, or measured K, S of the pigment in oil.

rose.material: quinacridone or madder lake (PV19 / PR83); organic
rose.note: Organic pigment: no CC0 constants. Needs n, k of the pigment crystal or measured K, S.

green.material: viridian, hydrated chromium oxide (PG18), a transparent green
green.note: No Cr2O3 or viridian constants in the CC0 database. Needs n, k 380-1550 nm.

dioxazine.note: Organic pigment: no CC0 constants. Needs n, k or measured K, S.

gesso.note: Chalk ground; k = 0 assumed (Ghosh's dispersion fit is for the transparent range). A gypsum (Italian) or acrylic (calcite + rutile) gesso would differ; gypsum is not in the CC0 database.

sources.reference: G. Ghosh. Dispersion-equation coefficients for the refractive index and birefringence of calcite and quartz crystals. Opt. Commun. 163, 95-102 (1999)
G. Ghosh. Dispersion-equation coefficients for the refractive index and birefringence of calcite and quartz crystals. Opt. Commun. 163, 95-102 (1999)

paper.note: Juntunen et al. measured microcrystalline cellulose at 1.10-1.65 um; the visible is the Cauchy fit extrapolated (n 1.56-1.60). Fibres (ribbons ~20 um wide) are treated as spheres: the absolute S is rough, the dependence on the filling index is the point. k = 0 assumed (no lignin, no sizing).

sources.reference: C. Juntunen, A. J. Rish, C. A. Anderson, Y. Sung. Refractive index measurement of pharmaceutical powders in the short-wave infrared range using index matching assisted with phase imaging. Powder Technol. 438, 119621-23149 (2024)

acrylic.material: acrylic polymer (PMMA as the stand-in for an acrylate copolymer)
acrylic.note: Bulk K is the clear film (S = 0). The per-surrounding K, S are the polymer as 0.15 um latex particles: in water, the wet emulsion; in air, an uncoalesced dried latex; in oil, nearly index-matched. 380-390 nm hold the 400 nm value.

sources.reference: 1) X. Zhang, J. Qiu, X. Li, J. Zhao, L. Liu. Complex refractive indices measurements of polymers in visible and near-infrared bands. Appl. Opt. 59, 2337-2344 (2020) (0.4-2 µm) 2) X. Zhang, J. Qiu, J. Zhao, X. Li, L. Liu. Complex refractive indices measurements of polymers in infrared bands. J. Quant. Spectrosc. Radiat. Transf. 252, 107063 (2020) (2-20 µm)
sources.comment: Normal temperature and pressure. Manufacturer: Tomson, China.

water.note: KM K = 2 alpha with alpha = 4 pi k / lambda (diffuse light); S = 0.

sources.reference: G. M. Hale and M. R. Querry. Optical constants of water in the 200-nm to 200-µm wavelength region. Appl. Opt. 12, 555-563 (1973) See also Segelstein 1981 for more recent data from the same group.

oil.note: No linseed constants in the CC0 database. n = 1.48 at 589 nm (OPTICS-SPEC) is assumed, with the dispersion of oleic acid (Jones et al., Cauchy B = 4.565e-3 um^2). K is goo's yellowing guess.

sources.reference: S. H. Jones, M. D. King, A. D. Ward. Atmospherically relevant core–shell aerosol studied using optical trapping and Mie scattering. Chem. Commun. 51, 4914-4917 (2015)
